steps.what: Read the prototype optomechanical drawings, tolerances and assembly requirements
Build the actual prototype optomechanical device and align its optical and mechanical components
Check prototype fit and alignment and physically correct assembly problems

tasks.design: Retain the physical prototype build and read its existing drawings from {DOCS} separately. A native drawing view is already the means of reading; no repeated record write, separate test report or machine-build interface is established by this build task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prototype construction involves actual alignment and fit of nonstandard components.
tasks.enabler_now: No specific software change is established for this physical build.
tasks.still_hard: Small mechanical deviations can alter optical alignment and require hands-on correction.
tasks.human_edge: The technician detects and corrects fit and alignment problems in the real assembly.
tasks.altitude: The build and drawing reading stay with the technician.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: nonstandard optomechanical prototype assembly requires physical fit and alignment work.

assumptions: The drawing lookup is separated and already uses the existing document view; no new lookup benefit is assumed.
A formal diagnostic result record belongs to the diagnostic task when actually performed; no unused build log is added here.
research_questions: Does local build practice require a separate traveller entry that should be counted before estimating another branch?

already_counted.description: All drawing reading, assembly and fit correction remain in s1 through s3.

incremental.description: No new process or upkeep is introduced.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. The actual drawing lookup is separated from physical assembly; no repeated entry, send or changed machine operation is demonstrated. All time is retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose processing steps with optical metrology

steps.what: Verify the diagnostic question, sample identity, instrument calibration, units and measurement method
outputs: verified diagnostic setup and sample metadata

steps.what: Perform microscopy, profilometry or ellipsometry measurements on the actual processing samples
inputs: verified diagnostic setup and sample metadata
outputs: actual instrument readings and measurement observations

steps.what: Transfer the actual instrument readings into the diagnostic analysis table
inputs: actual instrument readings and measurement observations
verified diagnostic setup and sample metadata

steps.what: Check the transferred readings and diagnose processing causes against the actual sample evidence
inputs: actual instrument readings and measurement observations

steps.what: Write and check the actual diagnostic finding with measurement limitations and source references

tasks.design: Test native export from {OTHER} optical metrology software into the existing {SPREADSHEET} analysis table before considering code. The technician captures sample metadata in s1, makes the measurements in s2 and checks exported values, units and missing readings in s4 before writing the existing diagnostic finding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instrument readings may be manually transcribed into the analysis table.
tasks.enabler_now: Compatible native exports can transfer readings with their sample and unit metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Calibration, sample artefacts and physical process causes need technical diagnosis.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises when a plausible numerical result is an invalid measurement.
tasks.altitude: Remove real second-system transcription while retaining metrology and diagnosis.

evidence.claim: DewesoftX records test data and produces reports; this demonstrates test-data output capability, not compatibility with a particular optical instrument.
Model knowledge: optical instrument exports require sample, unit and missing-value validation before diagnostic use.

assumptions: Shares are hypotheses for a manual instrument-to-analysis transcription branch; existing automatic acquisition runtime yields no labour saving.
OTHER means optical metrology instrument software.
The technician produces sample ID, instrument ID, method, calibration version and units in s1; the actual instrument produces readings in s2.
Missing metadata or incompatible exports stop for manual transcription and repair in retained s4; no free extraction is assumed.
The diagnostic finding already goes into the actual investigation record; no new trailing log is introduced.
research_questions: Can native export reproduce each sample's values, units and missing readings without manual re-keying?

already_counted.description: Verify metadata in s1 and check transferred readings, perform manual fallback and diagnose causes in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised export mapping and unit regression checks.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Native transfer removes 15 transcription hours less 1 upkeep, net 14. Cautious case: an instrument-specific export omits most sample metadata and requires manual reconstruction, leaving only 3 hours of compatible reading transfer removed and 2 net; fallback work consumes the rest of the nominal transfer benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Design or modify the fixture drawing for the actual parts, constraints and assembly access
Prepare the actual fixture materials and tools from the checked design
Build or physically modify the fixture used to assemble the parts
Check fixture fit, part location and assembly access and physically correct problems

tasks.design: Reuse native {OTHER} CAD fixture blocks for recurring baseplates and standard locating components while the technician designs the actual geometry and clearances. OTHER denotes CAD software; the drawing save is ordinary author work and physical building and fit checks remain unchanged.
tasks.previous_blocker: Standard baseplates and locator details may be redrawn in otherwise custom fixture designs.
tasks.enabler_now: Verified native CAD blocks can supply recurring geometry without choosing the fixture's functional layout.
tasks.still_hard: Clamping forces, tolerances and assembly access depend on the real parts.
tasks.human_edge: The technician judges whether the fixture constrains parts correctly without damaging them.
tasks.altitude: Reuse a small amount of standard geometry inside fixture design.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native CAD blocks can reuse standard fixture components while custom geometry and fit remain technical work.

assumptions: Only recurring standard-component drawing is removed from s1, not fixture design judgement.
The technician validates reused component dimensions within s1; no new drawing approval or unused build log is added.
Existing CAD blocks already used today cannot earn the same saving again.
research_questions: How much actual design entry is recurring standard geometry rather than new locating decisions?

already_counted.description: Check reused dimensions and correct design geometry in s1 and retain the actual physical fit check in s4.

incremental.description: Amortised dimensional checks and library-version maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Repeated component geometry removes 35*0.06=2.1 hours less 0.5 upkeep, net 1.6. Cautious case: unusual small optical parts require a bespoke fixture and only 0.6 hours of standard baseplate geometry is reusable, leaving 0.1 net; design decisions and physical building stay retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Verify the drawing revision, dimensions, datums, material and required machining allowance
Construct the cutting-line geometry and offsets from the verified drawing dimensions
Lay out the actual cutting lines on the stock using drafting and marking tools
Check the cutting lines against datums, dimensions and allowance and correct errors

tasks.design: Use native {OTHER} CAD offsets and dimensions to construct the cutting layout from technician-verified datums and allowances. OTHER denotes drafting software; the technician still transfers the lines onto actual stock and checks the marked result, with no automated machining or machine release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated offset and line construction can be performed manually before marking stock.
tasks.enabler_now: Native CAD geometry can reproduce exact offsets from verified dimensions.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong datum selection or physical transfer can make mathematically correct geometry unusable.
tasks.human_edge: The technician relates the drawing to the actual stock and machining process.
tasks.altitude: Remove repeated geometric construction while retaining physical layout.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native CAD offset and dimension tools can construct exact cutting-line geometry.

assumptions: Shares describe an unmeasured branch that still constructs offset geometry manually; existing automatic drafting earns no further saving.
The technician produces revision, units, datums, dimensions and allowance in s1; missing dimensions stop for manual reconstruction and verification.
Manual geometry repair is retained in s1 and s4 and reduces benefit in the cautious case.
The marked layout is the actual task output; no unused trailing record is added.
research_questions: Can the verified drawing dimensions generate the intended offsets without rebuilding most geometry?

already_counted.description: Verify and reconstruct source dimensions in s1 and check and repair the marked layout in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100. Native construction removes 20 geometry hours less 1 upkeep, net 19. Cautious case: an incomplete legacy drawing requires manual datum and offset reconstruction, leaving only 3 hours of simple parallel-line construction removed and 2 net; reconstruction consumes the rest of the nominal geometry benefit.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep physical optical work and technical checks while reducing verified drawing and data-transfer mechanics.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish automatic runtime from removed human transcription
role.ambitious_version: A photonics technician uses reliable native drafting and measurement outputs while retaining hands-on alignment and diagnosis.
